statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20% at the floor of the watch band while Stress stays extreme at 80%.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Tail has fallen to the bottom of the watch band because roughly 72% of the intraday range has been retraced, crude has pared most of its gain and VIX is off its high. One narrow danger window is flagged for 14:00-15:00Z on Sep 29, when JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence both print and the forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces roughly 72% of its intraday range as crude pares its gain; Tail eases to the watch-band floor with Stress still extreme
body: As of the 16:00Z clock-hour the Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,369.93, down 238.21 points or 0.78%, after a gap-down open at 30,426.63 from Friday's 30,608.13 close. The session traded down to 30,081.06 and has since recovered about 289 points, retracing roughly 72% of the 30,480.40-30,081.06 intraday range and returning to the opening level, so the retracement is deep rather than shallow and repeated extension after failed pullbacks has not been observed. The energy impulse that drove the early risk-off has faded materially: WTI is $92.91, up 0.54%, against about 3% higher an hour earlier, and Brent is $105.30, up 0.94%, against roughly 4% earlier, after Saudi East-West pipeline shipments resumed and markets priced a less severe supply shock even though President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. VIX is 16.15, up 8.61% from 14.87 but below its 16.62 session high and still a low absolute level. NQ futures trade 30,555.75, down 1.08%, about 198 points off their 30,357.75 low. The unresolved stress source is rates: the 10-year yield is 5.26% against a 5.18% prior close and close to its 5.27% high. Internals stay dispersed rather than uniformly weak, with Nvidia up 3.13% at 232.12 near its session high after authorising a record $150 billion buyback, against continued weakness in ARM and Qualcomm. Shared Finviz context collected at 14:34Z is both partial and, at this assessment time, older than the 90-minute freshness threshold, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled non-real-time and were used only as weak confirming context showing broad sector weakness with high semiconductor dispersion. Taken together this reads as an orderly, dispersion-driven drawdown that is actively mean-reverting inside a high-yield regime, which places Tail at 20% with Stress at 80% and Confidence at 88%.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours ran from a calm late-Friday regime with Tail near 8-14% into an overnight repricing that lifted Tail into the 21-24% watch band from the 03:00Z hour onward, while Stress climbed from 68% to the mid-80s. Two hours printed in the elevated band: 09:00Z at 26% during the European morning as crude extended, and 14:00Z at 27% as the US cash session traded down toward its low. Confidence improved steadily from 77% to 88% as live price-path and cross-asset evidence accumulated. Historical entries are the values published at the time and are not restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the lower half of the watch band through the remainder of the US cash session, with the 19:00Z power hour the highest slot at 24% on an unfilled gap-down day. After the 20:00Z close the conditional path eases into the low band through the post-close and Asian hours, on the explicit assumption that no fresh US-Iran or Strait of Hormuz headline arrives, while Stress stays high on the $105 Brent and 5.26% yield backdrop. The watch band returns from 08:00Z as European cash hours transmit the rate move, and the single elevated slot falls at 14:00Z on Sep 29, when JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence both print inside the first half hour of US cash trade. Forecast values are conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.
